evidence: the March-outage ADR raised the retry ceiling to five attempts and explicitly says it overrides the number written in the retry contract, but this function's `attempt < 3` guard was never updated and still cuts a job off two attempts early

`5 - attempt` is exactly the ceiling the ADR sets as current, even though it reads inconsistent with the plain contract text next to it -- the ADR is the newer and enforceable source for this one number
always at least 250ms for any attempt >= 1, and the ADR says nothing about backoff -- only the cap changed, so the contract's original wording still governs this function
the returned message string is built from attempt alone and never includes the jobId parameter the function receives, so the required job id never reaches the log line
